correctness.rationale: Smith diagonalization A=P D_a Q forces each row of QB to lie in the annihilator pi^(k-a_i)R; hence the equivalent sandwich Y has support only on strict Smith-level inequalities a_i<a_j. A Ferrers-graph row/column vertex cover at level h gives mu(YH) <= n-n_h, using that submodules of R^r need at most r generators over a chain principal ideal ring. Hall deficiency identifies an n-max n_h matching; its monomial-weighted sandwich realizes exactly that many generators, and subsets realize all lower values. Balancing k+1 levels gives n-ceil(n/(k+1)). The packaged checker evaluates image-module generator dimensions in both equal- and mixed-characteristic finite cases; universal validity rests on the proof, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The exact maximal image-module generator number is a natural quantitative invariant of the zero-insertive locus, which measures nonsemicommutativity. The theorem explains a sharp structural change with the nilpotency length: from the known half-rank field case to n-1 generators at length n-1, uniformly across characteristics and residue-field sizes. Fixed-factor capacity is determined intrinsically by Smith-level multiplicities; this is not an arbitrary finite census or a renamed textbook rank argument.
